input: Reupholster the dining room chair cushions

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: The number of chairs and whether the task includes just the seat pad or also the back rest changes the scale of effort, materials needed, and time required significantly.
Whether this is a solo DIY project or involves hiring a professional upholsterer changes the entire approach, cost, and skill requirements.
A specific budget cap determines whether the user buys premium fabric, reuses existing foam, or opts for budget materials — and whether DIY is even the right path.
The current condition of the cushions (worn fabric only vs. damaged foam/springs underneath) determines how much stripping and rebuilding is needed before new fabric is applied.
The style, pattern, and material of the new fabric (e.g., velvet, linen, vinyl, patterned vs. solid) is the central creative decision and drives the entire material-sourcing step.
Knowing what tools and supplies the user already owns (staple gun, fabric scissors, batting, etc.) determines what still needs to be purchased or borrowed before starting.
Understanding the user's finish-quality standard — a quick refresh vs. a polished, professional-looking result — shapes how detailed the instructions and technique guidance needs to be.

gold.taskTitle: Reupholster dining room chair cushions yourself
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to reupholster the cushions on their dining room chairs, which could involve selecting fabric, removing old material, and attaching new upholstery.

questions.title: How many chairs are you reupholstering in total?
questions.description: Determines the full scope — number of seat pads, amount of fabric to buy, and total time investment.

questions.title: Are you doing this yourself or hiring a professional?
questions.description: Decides whether the plan focuses on DIY technique guidance or on finding and briefing an upholsterer.

questions.title: What is your total budget for this project?
questions.description: Sets limits on fabric quality, foam replacement, and any tools that need to be purchased.

questions.title: What condition are the cushions in right now?
questions.description: Determines whether only the fabric needs replacing or if the foam, batting, or frame also require repair or rebuilding.

questions.title: What fabric type or style are you aiming for?
questions.description: Drives material sourcing — e.g., durable performance fabric, velvet, linen, patterned, or solid — and must match the room's aesthetic.

questions.title: Which tools or supplies do you already have on hand?
questions.description: Identifies gaps in the user's toolkit — staple gun, fabric scissors, batting, pliers — so the shopping list is accurate and nothing is assumed.

questions.title: How polished does the finished result need to look?
questions.description: Sets the quality bar — a quick functional refresh versus neat, taut, professional-grade upholstery — which shapes how detailed the technique guidance should be.
